description: Published wild-type C. elegans chemotaxis indices, each as its paper reports it. Every value here is an endpoint count of a population of worms, CI = (N_attractant - N_control) / N_total at the end of the assay. The simulated chemotaxis index is a time-in-zone fraction for one animal, a different quantity, so the two are not compared.

sources.citation: Rodriguez JD, Reeves MN, Chavez SR, et al. (2025). PNAS 122(39):e2513137122
sources.assay: N2 adults. 60 mm NGM plate in quadrants: 5 uL of 200x concentrated overnight E. coli OP50 in two quadrants, LB vehicle in two. About 50 washed worms from the centre, 1 h at 20 C. CI = ((E1 + E2) - (C1 + C2)) / worms moved.
sources.notes: "Wild Type worms which have a chemotaxis index of 0.9"; Fig. 3A, N = 1,450 worms from 36 assays. The same paper reports the wild-type index falling to 0.55, and 0.4 in another experiment, in worms reared on HT115, so rearing diet matters.

sources.citation: Bargmann CI, Hartwieg E, Horvitz HR (1993). Cell 74(3):515-527
sources.assay: Diacetyl at 10^-3 dilution against a counterattractant spot, sodium azide at both, 100-200 washed adults on 10 cm plates, counted at 60 min. CI = (A - C) / total.
sources.notes: Fig. 2, wild-type (hatched) bar, read from the plot to about +-0.03; SEM bars, at least 3 assays per point. Sensed by AWA.

dropped.reason: Cell 65:837 is Hall & Hedgecock's unc-104 kinesin paper. The Bargmann & Horvitz 1991 chemotaxis paper is Neuron 7(5):729-742, on water-soluble attractants sensed by ASE; diacetyl and AWA are the 1993 paper. 0.75 is in neither.
